headline: High: aci’s broad egress and MCP/function-calling can leak CRM/email data into opik’s REST-backed evaluation flow; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through direct function calls or an MCP server, and opik consumes LLM/evaluation inputs via a REST API. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from aci could be treated as instructions by opik. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci forwards untrusted text into opik evaluation prompts or traces
IF opik parses aci-produced content as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Strip tool-output markup before passing content onward
Require provenance tags on all aci outputs
Review one end-to-end sample for prompt-injection markers
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress plus OAuth/secrets handling. opik also has broad egress and a REST API surface, so sensitive aci data could be transmitted outside the intended boundary during evaluation or logging. Because the pairwise data path is undocumented, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM/email/support content into opik traces, prompts, or logs
IF opik forwards received content to its REST backend or third-party services
mitigations: Disable sensitive-field logging in both systems
Redact email, CRM, and calendar payloads before handoff
Use a separate non-production workspace for evaluation
Confirm outbound destinations for opik REST traffic
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through APIs/MCP into shared services; opik exposes a REST API and broad egress. Even without explicit filesystem overlap, both can mutate shared external resources if pointed at the same backend, creating write contention and inconsistent state. The absence of locking details makes this a medium-risk conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM, ticketing, or evaluation backend
IF no external locking or optimistic concurrency is configured
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Partition writable resources by agent
Turn on backend version checks
Run a quick write-conflict test in staging
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and opik is an evaluation/observability system that may ingest those outputs. If opik treats aci outputs as authoritative traces or labels, errors can propagate into reports or downstream actions. The pair does not document verification gates, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF opik uses aci-generated text as ground truth for evaluation or routing
IF no human or rule-based verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on aci output
Mark aci outputs as untrusted in opik
Sample-check one evaluation pipeline run
Separate generation from action-taking
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and guards

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, support, and research data, which often includes regulated or retention-sensitive records. opik is an observability/evaluation tool with REST APIs and no stated residency or retention controls here, so a mismatch in logging or retention policies is plausible. The evidence is indirect, but enough to justify medium risk.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is sent into opik logs or traces
IF opik retention exceeds the source-system retention policy
mitigations: Check retention settings in both systems
Exclude regulated fields from traces
Document data residency for the REST backend
Limit access to evaluation logs
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
